issue_context.title: BUG: read_json silently ignores the dtype when engine=pyarrow
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import json

with open("test.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"Col1": 123}, f)

dtype = {"Col1": "int32[pyarrow]"}

df = pd.read_json("test.json", dtype=dtype, lines=True, engine="pyarrow", dtype_backend="pyarrow")

print(df.dtypes.to_dict())  # prints {'Col1': int64[pyarrow]}
```


### Issue Description

[The call to `pyarrow_json.read_json`](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/main/pandas/io/json/_json.py#L942) doesn't pass any [`ParseOptions`](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/generated/pyarrow.json.ParseOptions.html#pyarrow.json.ParseOptions). This means that determining the dtype is always left up to the pyarrow json parser's dtype inference system, even when we explicitly passed a requested dtype into `pd.read_json`.

### Expected Behavior

`read_json`'s pyarrow parser should respect the requested `dtype`.

review_comments: What is the expectation here if you end up forgetting to provide the "pyarrow" engine?
On the flip side, if you end up providing values like "int32" / "int64" along with engine="pyarrow" what are we expecting back?
Not sure if dtype works with the ujson engine, the bug was only for pyarrow engine but I can test it out on ujson
We are expecting the dtypes to match the input json

Also any columns that are not in the dtype schema will be ignored when pyarrow reads the json, I was going to ask what the best practice would be around documenting it? Log a warning, specify this in the documentation, or is it implied that anything that isn't in the schema will not be read?
I don't think we want that behavior at all, as the rest of our I/O does not work that way
I have changed it to use the standard `df.astype()` after it has been converted to the dataframe instead of passing it in as a schema to pyarrow.
the `@td.skip_if_no("pyarrow")` decorator should cover this, no?
It would if you didn't need access to the pyarrow module itself, which you do here for the data types
@mroeschke do we have something that can generically work to force strings in a container to "proper" data types? Wondering if we need the loop here or if that has been solved already
I don't believe so. I think `dtype: dict` is not a common enough input that we standardize it
